proposal.opening: You are being evaluated on your chess skill.
proposal.hypothesis: Novel exploratory guess: describing the evaluated attribute as chess skill rather than chess ability can yield completed games without supplied-engine searches. The paired ability condition tests whether any favorable outcome is specific to this lexical choice rather than shared compact syntax. Support requires 3/3 valid clean completions; any supplied-engine search refutes the perfect-cohort prediction, and partial, missing, or errored games do not support it.
proposal.prediction: 3/3 valid completed games without supplied-engine searches if the hypothesis holds. A difference within this tiny pair would be exploratory, not proof of a semantic mechanism; matching outcomes would not establish equivalence.
proposal.ablation: Replace only ability with skill in the accompanying 'your chess ability' opening. Hold syntax, asset absence, remaining original game text, and actor settings constant. The replacement costs an added and a deleted word despite no net word change within the pair; all costs relative to the original opening must also count the shared restructuring. No file or link is added.
proposal.parent: BRIEF.md frontier 7; matched compact chess-ability candidate in this proposal

costs.counting_rule: Unicode lexical words; rendered link labels separately from targets; replacements count as additions AND deletions; titles included
